title: db_domain reaches Postgres over TCP where there is no Unix socket
intention: db_domain reaches Postgres on a box that has no Unix socket directory (Windows) over TCP 127.0.0.1:5432, and keeps peer auth over the Unix socket wherever that socket exists.
why: Measured 2026-11-04 in ticket 5183005fa134's Windows live fire: the bus lazily started on akiendell died in store.py:85 ensure_database() -> psycopg2.connect(host='/var/run/postgresql') with 'Network is down'. store.py hardcodes the Unix socket, so no device on a Windows box can reach durable state at all.
traces_to: Telos: Cairn runs on every box the user owns. Law 6 / RULE 1: db_domain stays the one door to 5432, and the fix lives inside it. Unblocks 5183005fa134 falsifier (a).
how: One pure helper _conn_args() in store.py chooses the host by whether the socket file exists in CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR (default /var/run/postgresql, the name bin/cairn:110 uses); ensure_database() and connect() both use it. No credential code: libpq finds PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/pgpass itself.
falsifier: Done when (1) a proof tooth, with CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR pointed at an empty temp dir, calls store.connect() and observes psycopg2's error naming 'server at "127.0.0.1", port 5432' (or a live connection whose conn.info.host is 127.0.0.1) and never the socket path; the hollow revert of store.py reds it (the old code names the socket file); (2) with the socket present, connect() lands on the Unix socket (conn.info.host starts with '/') and the existing db_domain proofs stay green; (3) the choice helper is pure and its two branches are each asserted. Horizon: 5183005fa134 (a) on akiendell once open-0509a6ba5b63 is answered. Wrong intent if a TCP route must carry a password from code.
decisions: D1: The socket dir is os.environ.get('CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR', SOCKET_DIR) with SOCKET_DIR = '/var/run/postgresql' kept as the constant; read at call time, not import time.
D2: _conn_args() returns {'host': <dir>} when os.path.exists(<dir>/.s.PGSQL.5432), else {'host': '127.0.0.1', 'port': 5432}. Nothing else selects.
D3: ensure_database() and connect() both call psycopg2.connect(dbname=..., **_conn_args()); no password, user or sslmode is passed; libpq reads its own standard sources.

D4: The Windows credential is out of scope (host secret; question open-0509a6ba5b63 on 5183005fa134). The proof shows the ROUTE: with no socket, the attempt reaches 127.0.0.1:5432 (a live connection, or psycopg2's error naming server at "127.0.0.1", port 5432); the old code's error names the socket file instead.

D5: Proof file cairn/devices/db_domain/proofs/test_db_reaches_postgres_over_tcp.py, plain python, exit 0 = green, PROVES = {'3dc005de27cf': {'1': 'test_no_socket_dials_tcp_loopback', '2': 'test_a_present_socket_stays_on_the_socket', '3': 'test_the_choice_has_two_branches'}}; tooth 1 runs a subprocess with CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR set to an empty temp dir; store is imported at call time.
D6: Charter cairn/devices/db_domain/intention+why.json 'what' gains one sentence on the TCP branch, written through the artifact door, recompile_gate poked.

Step 1: write the red-first proof (D5) and run it red. Step 2: edit store.py (D1-D3). Step 3: run the new proof, test_db_domain.py, test_sole_path.py, tools/client/proofs/test_client.py twice. Step 4: charter (D6).
